BioNova Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the BioNova Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a landline or the button provided if on the webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss BioNova Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are John Harlan, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Rivera, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial; Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing; and Karen Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Harlan, CEO of BioNova Therapeutics.

John Harlan, CEO:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. BioNova Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by pivotal regulatory milestones, robust commercial execution, proactive strategies around our patent portfolio, meaningful clinical advancements, focused R&D investments, impactful business development activities, accelerating growth in emerging markets, and solid cash generation. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities across immuno-oncology, gene therapies, and rare diseases.

We are particularly excited about NovaCure™, our next-generation PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, and its potential to transform first-line metastatic non-small cell lung cancer treatment while expanding our leadership in the IO space.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Michael Chen, CFO:
Thank you, John. As John mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2.8 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong uptake of NovaCure in oncology, label expansions across our portfolio, and double-digit growth in emerging markets, partially offset by expected biosimilar pressures on legacy assets.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $520 million, or $1.35 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $650 million, or $1.68 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1.4 billion, reflecting continued investments in R&D to advance our late-stage pipeline and manufacturing scale-up, alongside marketing spend to support NovaCure's commercial launches.

Let me provide more color on our R&D expense and pipeline investment priorities. For the third quarter, R&D expense totaled $480 million, up 22% year-over-year. This reflects accelerated investment in late-stage clinical programs like NovaCure's ongoing trials and next-generation modalities such as ADCs and gene therapies, offset by partnership milestones. As a percentage of net product revenues, R&D was at 23%, within our target range, aligning with peers ramping for blockbuster potential. Discovery and preclinical accounted for 27% of spend, driven by our AI platform yielding new oncology targets. Clinical-stage took 53%, with Phase III trials leading on NovaCure analogs and bispecifics. Manufacturing and regulatory prep was 14%, and the rest supported real-world evidence for expansions.

On geographic revenue breakdown and emerging market growth, the U.S. contributed 55% or $1.54 billion, up 13% YoY, led by NovaCure prescriptions and biosimilars. Europe was 25% or $700 million, flat reported but up 3% constant currency amid pricing pressures offset by rare disease strength. Japan and established APAC were 10% or $280 million, up 11% on reimbursements. Emerging markets shone at 10% or $280 million, up 28% YoY and 35% constant currency—their 12th straight strong quarter. China grew 38% on NovaCure NRDL inclusion, Latin America 30% via biosimilar tenders, India/MENA 25%, with investments in local manufacturing and access programs positioning EM for 16% of total revenues by 2025.

Cash flow and balance sheet remain strong. Operating cash flow was $480 million, up 30% YoY, driven by NovaCure sales and DSO at 48 days. Free cash flow hit $340 million after $140 million capex for gene therapy facilities. We ended with $3.2 billion in cash equivalents, net cash of $1.5 billion, current ratio 2.9x. This supports our pipeline and M&A.

On patent cliff exposure and life cycle management, our top assets—NovaCure at 42% of sales, NovaFlex immunology at 23%, NovaHeart CV at 14%—face U.S. LOE in 2027-2029. Without action, $3.5-4.5 billion risk by 2030, but our LCM has preserved 75% via $3 billion invested over five years. Label expansions like NovaCure in new combos add $1 billion peak; formulations extend patents; biosimilar JVs capture erosion; pricing strategies limit net erosion to 6%.

Business development was robust: $275 million upfront for ONC-ADC-472 ADC in-license, $950 million GeneX acquisition for DMD gene editing, expanded Regeneron bispecific partnership with $320 million commitment. These add $4.5 billion NPV, aligning with M&A trends.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $11.2-11.8 billion, EPS $5.80-6.20 non-GAAP.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Emily Rivera, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

Dr. Emily Rivera, Chief Medical Officer:
Thank you, Michael. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, our flagship NovaCure bispecific T-cell engager in HER2-positive solid tumors reported positive Phase 3 topline: 48% ORR vs 22% chemo, PFS 11.2 vs 5.8 months, HR 0.42. BLA submission Q4 2024, PDUFA Q3 2025. In hematology, NovaGene-205 CRISPR for hemophilia A showed 52 IU/dL Factor VIII at 12 months, bleeding down 87%; Phase 3 starts Q1 2025. Early ADC NBT-312 hit 35% ORR. We expect three readouts and two filings in 2025. Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:
Thank you, Emily. We are making significant strides in our early-stage research. Our AI-driven platform with Insilico nominated STING agonists and KRAS PROTACs, aligning with ADC and gene editing trends. Discovery spend supports three new INDs, with modalities like degraders cutting timelines 40%. We've de-risked via partnerships, positioning for $5 billion peak sales. Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial:
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with NovaCure total Rx up 28% YoY to 1.3 million TRx, NRx 37% to 480,000, market share 19% in NSCLC. Sales force hit 8.5 calls/day via AI Veeva CRM, cost per TRx $140. U.S. 73% of Rx up 34%, digital 45% impressions, EU 23% growth, EM 58%. ROI 5x via MMM, Precision Promo AI lifted NRx 28%. Adherence 88% on patient apps. We guide 27% NRx growth FY24. Next, Tom Reilly will discuss our manufacturing operations.

Tom Reilly, Head of Manufacturing:
Thank you, Lisa. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity utilization at 92% across Devens and Singapore sites, with 18% yield gains from continuous processing on mAbs and AAVs. Supply chain resilient, 95% on-time via diversified APIs amid inflation. Key priorities include scaling NovaGene-45 commercial lots and LNP for siRNAs, with $150 million capex for sterile fill-finish. No disruptions, focused on 99.9% compliance.

Karen Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Thank you, Tom. We continue to work closely with regulatory agencies. This quarter marked a pivotal time with three major approvals and two label expansions. NovaCure got FDA full approval for first-line NSCLC high PD-L1, Phase 3 data: PFS 14.2 months, HR 0.72, ORR uplift 22%; EMA CHMP positive, launch Q1 2025, $650 million incremental 2025 U.S. revenue. NovaGene-45 accelerated approval for SMA1, 92% event-free survival vs Zolgensma; $250 million FY25. NovaShield pediatric obesity expansion, 17.5% weight loss; BioSim-Bev EMA approval. These add $2.8 billion peak sales, de-risk seven 2025 readouts. Bolstered team with ex-FDA hires.

Now, I'll hand the call back to John Harlan.

John Harlan, CEO:
Thank you, Karen. In summary, these achievements across regulatory, commercial, pipeline, and operations position us strongly. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, the question-and-answer session has begun. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the NovaCure NSCLC label expansion, can you elaborate on the competitive positioning versus Keytruda and launch readiness?

Karen Lee, Head of Regulatory Affairs:
Thanks, John. The Phase 3 NOVALUNG-301 data showed a 28% PFS improvement to 14.2 months and 22% ORR uplift, with HR 0.72 and IRAEs at 18% Grade 3/4—on par with Opdivo. This positions us for 15-20% share in the $12 billion 1L NSCLC market. Sales force at 450 reps, patient programs ready; U.S. Q1 2025 launch on track, EMA year-end.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez, J.P. Morgan:
Great, thanks. Michael, on guidance—how does EM growth and BD inflows factor into the updated FY revenue midpoint?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Hi Maria. EM's 28% growth contributes 2 points to top-line, with China NRDL driving NovaCure volumes. BD added $180 million upfront from Takeda out-license, plus milestones. Midpoint $11.5 billion reflects 18% growth, conservative on FX and biosimilars, with LCM offsetting cliffs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim, Morgan Stanley:
Thanks. Emily, thoughts on the hemophilia A interim data durability and Phase 3 enrollment risks?

Dr. Emily Rivera, Chief Medical Officer:
David, the HEMO-CURE Phase 2 showed sustained 52 IU/dL Factor VIII at 12 months, 87% bleeding reduction, minimal immunogenicity via Cas9 shielding. Phase 3 enrolls 150 globally Q1 2025, leveraging RMAT and PRIME. Risks mitigated by multi-regional design, on track for BLA 2026.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Patel with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Alex Patel, Bank of America:
Thanks. Lisa, with payer scrutiny, how sustainable are the 5x promo ROI and NRx growth for NovaCure?

Lisa Wong, Head of Commercial:
Alex, sustainability comes from omnichannel: 92% top-decile reach, AI targeting 27% NRx lift. Refill rates 78%, value-based pilots with PBMs on PFS outcomes. Biosimilar shifts redeployed reps; guide 25-30% FY24 NRx amid $50B PD-1 market.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Chen with Citi. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen, Citi:
Quick one for Michael: details on patent cliff mitigation—any updates to Zorvix analogs' timeline?

Michael Chen, CFO:
Sarah, NovaCure's U.S. COM expiry 2027, but expansions to endometrial/breast add orphan exclusivity to 2034. Settled 14 ANDAs to 2028 entry, EU SPC to 2031. Biosimilar JV captures 25% erosion; $4.5 billion LCM peaks maintain 7-9% 2025 growth.

Operator:
That concludes the question-and-answer session. I'll now turn the call back over to John Harlan for closing remarks.

John Harlan, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the BioNova Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
